scale.1: Present but weak or incompletely applied

criteria.title: Core problem
criteria.two_point_standard: The title, abstract, and opening introduction identify the same specific problem.

criteria.title: Load-bearing claim
criteria.two_point_standard: The manuscript can be condensed into one defensible proposition.

criteria.title: Contribution statement
criteria.two_point_standard: The contribution identifies debate position, unresolved condition, paper's move, and limit.

criteria.title: Literature function
criteria.two_point_standard: Each core source has a distinguishable role in the argument.

criteria.title: Core definition
criteria.two_point_standard: The definition specifies object, relation, limit, consequence, and failure.

criteria.title: Conceptual work
criteria.two_point_standard: The central concept performs at least three distinct, necessary tasks.

criteria.title: Conditions and failures
criteria.two_point_standard: Each condition rules out an identifiable counterfeit or counter-structure.

criteria.title: Testing by cases
criteria.two_point_standard: Cases test precise conditions and yield consequences for the theory.

criteria.title: Objection structure
criteria.two_point_standard: Objections are grouped by pressure, stated strongly, and answered with warranted concessions.

criteria.title: Paragraph actions
criteria.two_point_standard: Every paragraph performs a recognizable primary argumentative action.

criteria.title: Inferential bridges
criteria.two_point_standard: Major transitions and conclusions disclose their mediating premises.

criteria.title: Conclusion boundaries
criteria.two_point_standard: The strength and scope of the conclusion match what was established.

cross_cutting_checks.title: Terminological stability
cross_cutting_checks.instruction: Complete a separate terminology ledger. This is required review, not a thirteenth scored criterion.

cross_cutting_checks.title: Evidence integrity
cross_cutting_checks.instruction: Verify citations, quotations, examples, and empirical or historical assertions against primary sources.
